title: Newly released documents suggest CIA did more post-9/11 waterboarding than previously acknowledged
summary_full: Declassified documents appear to support belief that waterboarding was more common and may have occurred beyond two acknowledged sitesNewly released documents suggest that the CIA waterboarded more detainees during the post-9/11 “war on terror” than previously acknowledged, utilizing a site north of Kabul, Afghanistan, for the practice of simulated drowning.The agency has acknowledged waterboarding three men: Abu Zubaydah, believed to be a high-ranking member of al-Qaida; Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, suspected architect of the 11 September 2001 attacks; and Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, accused of planning the 2000 bombing of a navy destroyer.
